# kiln v0.8.0

v0.8.0 routes every guest-to-host call through one `host_call`, which fixes GHSA-hcpp-639v-fw55 (low), adds the P3 cooperative-thread built-ins and runs the upstream Component Model WAST suite on meld-fused output. All 50 artifacts scoped to v0.8.0 in rivet are verified; v0.7.3 already shipped SR-81, SR-83, SR-85, SR-91, SR-94, SR-96 and SR-97 from this scope.

## Security fix (GHSA-hcpp-639v-fw55, #669)
Through v0.7.3 the routes from a guest to a host import disagreed:
- a WASI import reached through `call_ref` or `return_call` discarded the host error and returned default results; no `cabi_realloc` buffer was allocated and an out-of-range return-area pointer did not trap;
- on the core-module route, dispatcher calls that return core values (`wasi:filesystem` descriptor calls, `input-stream.read`) left the return area unwritten and pushed a stray operand;
- misaligned return-area pointers and `cabi_realloc` results were accepted where wasmtime traps.

v0.8.0 sends `call`, `call_indirect`, `call_ref` and `return_call` through one `host_call` that lowers results into the canonical return area, allocates returned buffers by one policy through the guest's `cabi_realloc`, propagates host errors, and traps on a misaligned or out-of-range return-area pointer or allocator result (SR-102). `get-arguments` and `get-directories` allocate their lists per call.

## Changes
- **P3 cooperative threads:** the nine `$root::[thread-*]` built-ins meld passes through run on the interpreter (SR-82, #668).
- **Collections panic safety:** `StaticVec`, `StaticMap` and `StaticQueue` drop each element exactly once when an element's `Drop` panics (SR-104, #676).
- **No write at guest address 0x100:** instantiation no longer overwrites 16 bytes at guest address 0x100; a data segment there survives (SR-105, #678).
- **Component Model WAST:** `cargo-kiln testsuite --run-cm-wast` runs the upstream suite on meld 0.68.0 output against a ratcheted baseline, in a non-required CI job (SR-93, #677). Today: 78 files, 5 pass, 32 refused by meld at fuse time, 41 fail; most failures are unresolved cross-component imports (SR-114, v0.9.0).
- **`poll` evidence:** engine-level tests show `poll` returns its ready indices in a `cabi_realloc` buffer and propagates an allocator trap (AD-WASIPOLL-001, #684).
- **CI:** four light jobs run on self-hosted runners for same-repo PRs, with a fail-closed fork guard (#675); hosted jobs are pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` (#683).
- **Dependencies:** cargo and GitHub Actions groups bumped (#664, #665). RUSTSEC-2026-0543 (chrono unmaintained) is ignored in `deny.toml`: chrono is used only by the build tooling and is not in the `kiln` binary on any release target; its removal is SR-115 (#682).

Verify the checksums with the exact identity:

```
cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.txt.cosign.bundle \
  --certificate-identity 'https://github.com/pulseengine/kiln/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v0.8.0' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  SHA256SUMS.txt
```

## Known limitations
- Read-style buffers (`input-stream.read`, `descriptor.read`) are reserved at an upper bound, so their `cabi_realloc` result is checked for alignment and start-in-memory only.
- No human reviewer is recorded on the v0.8.0 rivet artifacts (`provenance.reviewed-by`); the review is to be recorded after the release.
- SR-40, SR-79 and SR-80 are verified but have no design-decision artifact yet.
- kiln has no witness MC/DC truth tables and no sigil attestation; release assets are covered by the cosign-signed `SHA256SUMS.txt` (SR-85).

## Falsification statement
This release is wrong if:
- a host import reached through `call`, `call_indirect`, `call_ref` or `return_call` returns default results after the host reported an error, or writes guest memory outside the canonical return area and the buffers `cabi_realloc` returned for that call;
- a misaligned or out-of-range return-area pointer or `cabi_realloc` result is accepted on any of those routes;
- a data segment at guest address 0x100 reads back changed after instantiation;
- a `StaticVec`, `StaticMap` or `StaticQueue` element is dropped twice, or never, when another element's `Drop` panics;
- `cosign verify-blob` with the identity above does not print `Verified OK` for this release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, or a release asset other than the signature material is missing from it.
